usageNotes: Use this to write a file into a running VM via the QEMU Guest Agent (qemu-guest-agent must be installed and running inside the VM). The caller needs the `VM.GuestAgent.FileWrite` or `VM.GuestAgent.Unrestricted` privilege on `/vms/{vmid}`. Content is capped at 60 KB per call; for larger files, write a loader script first and pull the payload from inside the guest.

examples.summary: Write a custom resolv.conf into a Linux VM

tips: The VM must be powered on and the guest agent service must be running — the call will fail with a timeout or error if the agent is not responsive.
`encode` defaults to true, which lets you pass plain text safely; only set it to false if you are pre-encoding content as base64 yourself.
The operation returns null on success; no UPID is issued — errors surface as HTTP 5xx/4xx immediately.
File ownership and permissions inside the guest are determined by the guest agent process user (typically root); adjust permissions with a follow-up exec call if needed.
The 60 KB (61440 byte) content limit applies to the raw string before base64 expansion; plan multi-part writes for larger payloads.
